warnings: No formal upper limit is set for pantothenic acid; UK guidance considers 200 mg per day or less from supplements unlikely to cause harm.
Very large doses (grams per day) can cause diarrhoea and stomach upset.
Pantethine for cholesterol should only be used with a doctor's advice, especially together with statins or other lipid medicines.
Check labels for duplicate B-complex, multivitamin or hair-skin-nails products; these also contain vitamin B6, niacin and biotin.
Topical dexpanthenol (creams, ointments) does not count toward the daily intake.
Burning, numb or tingling feet need a doctor's check-up; they are more often caused by diabetes, B12 or B1 problems than by low B5.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
